text.tspan: A signed JWT cannot be un-signed, so revocation is a DATABASE fact instead — a row in token_blacklist and/or sessions.is_active set to false. Every path below writes one, the other, or both.
shouldNotFilter() exempts only /api/guest/** plus login and the two register paths, so
JWTAuthenticationFilter runs ahead of every call below, and SecurityConfig maps /api/** to authenticated.
Both are drawn once, in PAYOFF.
CASE 1 — POST /api/auth/logout ends only the session the caller is using.
[Authorization header absent or not a Bearer value]
DEFENSIVE ONLY — a tokenless call to /api/** is stopped by JwtAuthenticationEntryPoint with a 401
ApiErrorResponse, so this 400 is unreachable through the live filter chain.
CASE 2 — POST /api/auth/logout-all ends every session this user has anywhere.
Only the CALLER's own JWT string reaches token_blacklist. The other devices' tokens are never seen by the server so they cannot be blacklisted by value — they die on the
CASE 3 — revoking one device from the session list.

No token_blacklist row and no Set-Cookie here — SessionAPI never holds the revoked device's JWT and must not clear the caller's own cookie. DELETE /api/auth/sessions/revokeAll repeats the last arm over every findByUserAndIsActive row and answers All sessions revoked
PAYOFF — the revoked token is replayed while it is still inside its exp window.

TIMING — revocation is immediate for the device that called logout (Caffeine put plus the token_blacklist row), but eventually consistent for other devices: their token can stay cached as valid for up to the 2-minute expireAfterWrite window before the sessions.is_active check is re-run against the DB. That cache lives in one JVM and holds 10000
entries, so it is not shared between instances.

BODY TYPES — logout and logout-all are declared ResponseEntity of String and SessionAPI is declared ResponseEntity of wildcard, yet every outcome except getAllSessions returns a bare String, so those bodies are text/plain sentences and not JSON. Only getAllSessions (SessionDTO list) and the filter's 401 (ApiErrorResponse) are JSON.
